Concise Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
• 40-year-old postpartum woman with sudden onset shortness of breath and tachycardia 4 weeks after Cesarean section; high suspicion for pulmonary embolism—referred immediately to hospital for evaluation.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Acute shortness of breath that began ~1 hour ago while seated watching TV.  
• Course: Sudden onset, unchanged over the hour.  
• Associated symptoms:
  – Dry cough started yesterday.  
  – Palpitations (“my heart…it’s really going”).  
  – Chest soreness on deep inspiration; C-section scar also tender.  
• Pertinent negatives (per transcript): No chest pain at rest, no sputum, no reported fever or leg pain/swelling.  
• Past medical/surgical: Cesarean section 4 weeks ago; no chronic illnesses reported.  
• Medications: Codeine for post-op pain (last dose ~1 week ago); no current regular meds.  
• Allergies: Ibuprofen — reaction not specified.  
• Family history: Mother with history of leg clots (DVT).  
• Social / preventive: Caring for 4-week-old infant at home; partner at work. Smoking/alcohol/universal postpartum prophylaxis not discussed.

Examination:
• Self-measured radial pulse: 30 beats in unspecified interval; clinician interpreted as ~120 bpm (tachycardia).  
• No other vitals or physical findings documented via video/phone.  
• No lower-limb findings assessed.

Impression:
• Primary: Pulmonary embolism (postpartum) – high likelihood given sudden dyspnea, tachycardia, recent C-section (major surgery + hypercoagulability), postpartum status, family history of DVT, and pleuritic discomfort on inspiration.  
• Secondary considerations:  
  1. Acute respiratory infection (viral or bacterial) – cough onset the day prior, but lacks fever or gradual progression.  
  2. Anxiety/panic episode – patient reports stress and palpitations, but organic risk factors favor PE.

Plan:
• Immediate self-transport to nearest Emergency Department (patient declined ambulance).  
• Take essentials for baby; travel promptly.  
• Hold further codeine until evaluated.  
• ED evaluation to include vitals, ECG, D-dimer, CT pulmonary angiography or V/Q scan, full blood count, and coagulation profile (per standard PE work-up).  
• Hospital to consider anticoagulation therapy if PE confirmed.  
• Educate patient on warning signs (worsening breathlessness, chest pain, syncope) and to call emergency services if symptoms escalate en route.  
• No further medications prescribed during tele-visit.  
• Follow-up: As per hospital discharge instructions; routine post-partum care to continue with obstetric team/primary care.

Quality checks:

● Missing/expected elements: Complete vital signs (BP, RR, SpO₂, temperature); description of ibuprofen allergy reaction; comprehensive medication list; smoking status; obstetric history details; explicit follow-up arrangement after hospital visit.  
● Transcript/DDx conflicts: Date of birth—patient states 20 Apr 1980; clinician repeats 1983. (Conflict noted.)  
● Transcript quality: Adequate for chief complaint, but lacks full ROS, vitals, and physical exam; minor audio gaps.
